items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: Then I went to Rene first, my first teacher, Kid Rene.

ctx.x: Excuse me, I was going to ask you more about when you first started on trumpet, if you had any real lessons or- No, when I first started, I just picked it up like that. You picked it up-
Then I went to Rene first, my first teacher, Kid Rene.
Did you ever take any lessons when they used a method book or anything?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: I have played second to Rene. I played second to Buddy too at times, you know.

ctx.x: Well, what about guys like Chris and Buddy and... Who was that guy? Chris and Buddy and Rene and all those, would you play any second trumpet to them ever?

I have played second to Rene. I played second to Buddy too at times, you know. Most of the time, sometimes they'd split, they'd get in, they'd had so much work to it was. At that time, they'd split the band, you see. They'd send me either with the bass and they'd hire out the different ones, you know. You know, on them spot jobs, and they needed trumpet player, well they'd hire me. In fact, Rene taken the liking to me, I started playing following his, and I guess that's about what it was, you see, and I couldn't…
Remember any of the guys that Rene would have in his band?

items.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20
items.q: Well, I like Rene. Kid Rene playing. I went to Rene for a while afterwards, you know?

ctx.x: Strictly music, I see. What did you take after any jazz musicians? And once you got some lessons, did you have anybody you liked?
Well, I like Rene. Kid Rene playing. I went to Rene for a while afterwards, you know? Oh, I see. He taught you some lessons, too. Yeah, I taught you some lessons, too.
